Carbon nanotube filled with water

A carbon nanotube filled with water, in water. The nanotube is a fixed molecule along the z axis, crossing the periodic boundary of the box, so that it is infinite; the water fills the inside of the tube, and the box around it.

The packed system (drag to rotate, scroll to zoom), built in the Julia section below.

Files: cnt.pdb, water.pdb, and the input file nanotube.inp.

The nanotube is an armchair (12,12) tube, with a radius of 8.14 Å, and 49.2 Å long (20 periods of 2.46 Å along its axis, 960 carbon atoms), built with the Julia code at the end of this page. Its length is the length of the box along z, so that the tube is continuous across the periodic boundary.

The numbers of molecules

The atoms of water can get no closer than tolerance (2 Å) to the atoms of the nanotube, so inside the tube they are within a radius of about 6 Å. A cylinder of this radius and 49.2 Å long has 5560 Å³, which would hold about 185 molecules at 1 g/mL; water confined in a tube this narrow is less dense, and 150 molecules are packed. Outside the tube, beyond a radius of 10.5 Å, the box of 40 × 40 × 49.2 Å has 61700 Å³, which holds 2060 molecules at 1 g/mL (0.0334 molecules per Å³).

Command line

#
# A carbon nanotube (armchair, (12,12), radius 8.14 Å) filled with water, in
# water (1 g/mL), in a periodic box. The nanotube is along z, and crosses the
# periodic boundary: it is infinite.
#
tolerance 2.0
output nanotube.pdb
pbc -20. -20. -24.6 20. 20. 24.6

# Uncomment to write only the initial placement of the molecules to the output file,
# without packing them (to check the constraints):
# check_initial_placement

# The nanotube, kept at the coordinates of the file
structure cnt.pdb
  number 1
  fixed 0. 0. 0. 0. 0. 0.
end structure

# Water inside the tube. The cylinders start at z = -100 with a length of 200,
# longer than the box: they cross the periodic boundary along z.
structure water.pdb
  number 150
  inside cylinder 0. 0. -100. 0. 0. 1. 6. 200.
end structure

# Water outside the tube
structure water.pdb
  number 2060
  outside cylinder 0. 0. -100. 0. 0. 1. 10.5 200.
end structure

The cylinders (center of one cap, axis, radius and length) are longer than the box: with periodic boundary conditions, the atoms are evaluated in the box, where only the side of the cylinders matters.

Check the initial placement first

Uncomment the check_initial_placement line of the input file, and run it as below (see Checking the initial placement): the initial placement is written to the output file (nanotube.pdb) in a fraction of a second (see it at the end of the Julia section). When the water is in the tube and around it, comment the line again, and run the packing.

Packing

packmol nanotube.inp

The packing takes a fraction of a second.

Julia

using Packmol, PDBToolscnt = structure_type("cnt.pdb"; number = 1, fixed = ([0., 0., 0.], [0., 0., 0.]))water_inside = structure_type("water.pdb";    number = 150,    constraints = [InsideCylinder([0., 0., -100.], [0., 0., 1.], 6., 200.)],)water_outside = structure_type("water.pdb";    number = 2060,    constraints = [OutsideCylinder([0., 0., -100.], [0., 0., 1.], 10.5, 200.)],)system = PackmolSystem([cnt, water_inside, water_outside];    output = "nanotube.pdb",    tolerance = 2.0,    unitcell = [40. 0. 0.; 0. 40. 0.; 0. 0. 49.2], # centered at the origin    check_initial_placement = true, # first, only the initial placement)packmol(system)system.status
:not_packed

The initial approximation, with the visualize function of PDBTools.jl (drag to rotate, scroll to zoom): the water is in the tube and around it, but molecules may overlap:

show_system(system) = visualize(get_atoms(system),    "resname CNT" => (style = :sticks, color = "gray"),    "water" => (style = :sticks, water = true);    unitcell = UnitCell(system.unitcell),    unitcell_origin = -sum(eachcol(system.unitcell)) / 2,)show_system(system)

Then the packing:

system.check_initial_placement = falsepackmol(system)show_system(system)

Building the nanotube

The nanotube is the rectangular cell of graphene (2.46 × 4.26 Å, with 4 carbon atoms) rolled into a cylinder: for an armchair (n, n) tube, n cells along the circumference, with the C–C bonds along it, and the tube periodic along its axis with a period of 2.46 Å:

using PDBToolsfunction build_nanotube(; n = 12, nz = 20, a = 2.46, d = 1.42)    cell = [(0.0, 0.0), (a / 2, d / 2), (a / 2, 3d / 2), (0.0, 2d)]    circumference = n * 3d    radius = circumference / (2π)    Lz = nz * a    atoms = Atom{Nothing}[]    for i in 0:nz-1, j in 0:n-1, (z, y) in cell        θ = 2π * (j * 3d + y) / circumference        push!(atoms, Atom(; name = "C", resname = "CNT", resnum = 1, chain = "A",            x = radius * cos(θ), y = radius * sin(θ), z = i * a + z - Lz / 2,            pdb_element = "C",        ))    end    return atomsendwrite_pdb("cnt.pdb", build_nanotube())

get_atoms(packmol_system::PackmolSystem)

Returns the atoms of the packed system, with their current coordinates.

PackmolSystem(structure_types::Vector{<:StructureType}; output::String, kwargs...)

Build a PackmolSystem directly from a vector of StructureTypes (see structure_type), without going through an input file.

packmol(input_file::String; options...) packmol(packmol_system::PackmolSystem; options...) packmol( system::SolutionBoxUS; output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., ) packmol( system::SolutionBoxUSC; concentration::Number, concentration_units::Union{Nothing,String} = nothing, output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., ) packmol( system::SolutionBoxUWI; ionic_concentration::Number=0.15u"mol/L", output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., ) packmol( system::Membrane; output="membrane.pdb", kwargs..., ) packmol(system::MembraneProtein; output = "membrane_protein.pdb", kwargs...)

Read a Packmol input file, run the packing optimization, and write the output.

structure_type(filename; number, constraints=Constraint[], tolerance=2.0, radius=nothing, fixed=nothing, center=:none, residue_numbering=-1, D=3, T=Float64)

Build a StructureType for number copies of the molecule read from the PDB file filename, without going through an input file.

packmol(system::MembraneProtein; output = "membrane_protein.pdb", kwargs...)

Builds and packs a membrane protein system, without writing an input file (as write_packmol_input followed by packmol).

packmol( system::Membrane; output="membrane.pdb", kwargs..., )

Builds and packs a lipid membrane system, without writing an input file.

packmol( system::SolutionBoxUSC; concentration::Number, concentration_units::Union{Nothing,String} = nothing, output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., )

Builds and packs a Solute + Solvent + Cossolvent system, without writing an input file.

packmol( system::SolutionBoxUS; output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., )

Builds and packs a Solute + Solvent system, without writing an input file.

packmol( system::SolutionBoxUWI; ionic_concentration::Number=0.15u"mol/L", output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., )

Builds and packs a Solute + Water + Ions system, without writing an input file.
